_: Hand-written half of /commands. build.mjs reads every command and its help text from omabox's latest release (crates/omabox/src/help.txt); this file adds a group, a line and examples. A command missing here still shows, under Other. Examples must be valid at that release (omabox help).

up.say: Start a box: headless and invisible unless you ask for a window, any screen size or several monitors, Omarchy's desktop, a plain Hyprland or a copy of your own, with your plugins, an isolated network or a save to start from.

down.say: End a box and everything in it. A session's box also goes when its agent exits.

ls.say: Every box: its mode, size, state, whether its bar is running (and how often it crashed), network, idle time and plugins. `--json` adds what each one tested: the Omarchy version, the theme, each plugin's commit.

path.say: Where a box lives on disk; its HOME is `<dir>/home`, so you can seed an app's data files there.

mode.say: Show or change a headless box's screen size and refresh rate while it runs.

monitor.say: Add, remove and list a headless box's monitors while it runs: any size, scale and place, a bar on each. `remove` is an unplug: its workspaces move to the others.

output.say: A screen goes and comes back under its own name, as a monitor that drops off on wake does, so you see what your shell and apps do then. `--cycles` stops at the first shell crash.

reload.say: A box keeps the Hyprland config it started with, so updating omabox never resets a running test. `reload` gives it this omabox's config.

save.say: Keep a box's HOME (an app signed in, a PIN, a library) so new boxes start from it.

saves.say: List the saves, or delete them.

run.say: Run any command inside a box. `-d` launches an app and returns; `--replace` restarts it after a rebuild. With no box up, a throwaway box runs the command and goes.

shot.say: A PNG of the screen, a region, one monitor, or one window's own pixels, even covered or on another workspace. `--changed` sends only what changed since the last shot, `--burst` a transition in frames.

pixel.say: The colour of a pixel on the screen, in a window or in a shot, as `#rrggbb`: no image tool of your own.

windows.say: The box's windows: where they are, which workspace, what covers them.

wait.say: Wait for a still screen, a window, a layer, a line in the accessibility tree, a log line, a notification or a command, instead of sleeping.

tree.say: A window's or a layer's accessibility tree, as text: ask before you look. On a layer it lists the text the shell draws, so a bar widget is read without a shot.

check.say: Visual checks: a scenario's checkpoints against a baseline, said same or changed.

record.say: A video of the box, with marks, captions, input drawn in and a contact sheet.

audio.say: Listens to a box with `--audio` and says whether it made a sound, when and how loud.

log.say: A box's logs: Hyprland's by default, or the shell's, the apps', a `run -d` job's, what apps notified, which omabox commands ran against it and by whom, and a desk box's autostart decisions. `-f` follows them.

events.say: What the box's Hyprland reported, stamped: mark a point, act, then read what came after or wait for one event.

gpu.say: GPU time of one box's processes, to see what your app costs to draw; `release` takes down the boxes on a GPU before it goes to a VM.

cpu.say: CPU and memory of a box's processes, per thread with `--threads`.

gdb.say: Every thread's backtrace of the box's Hyprland or shell, hung or stopped too; `--watch` catches a crash into `omabox log gdb`.

keys.say: Key combos for Hyprland binds and the focused app, any Unicode text, or a password from your environment, never on a command line.

click.say: Click in screen, window or screenshot coordinates. `--steps` travels there, hovering what it crosses; `--mod` holds ctrl, shift or alt.

drag.say: Press, move, hold, release: sliders, selections, drag and drop.

scroll.say: Scroll there, up, down or sideways, as a mouse wheel's notches or a touchpad's smooth scroll; `--mod super` for Omarchy's SUPER+wheel binds.

pointer.say: Raw pointer moves, button presses, scrolls and pauses, for what `click` and `drag` don't cover.

lua.say: Lua in the box's Hyprland, printing what it returns (tables as JSON). Set an option with `hl.config`; `hyprctl keyword` sets nothing in a box.

restart-shell.say: Reload the box's Omarchy shell after you edit a plugin; it says why a plugin did not load.

peek.say: A live, view-only window of any box on workspace 9, opened without taking your focus.

keys-to-box.say: For an interactive box: SUPER keys go to it while its window has focus and the pointer is over it.

clip.say: Your clipboard into an interactive box, once, or the box's back to you. Never for agents.

env.say: Exports that point Wayland tools on your side at a box, so their windows open in it.

ports.say: Every box's servers, and who has each port on your `127.0.0.1`: that box, another box, one of your own processes, or nothing yet. When a dev server says the address is in use, this names who has it.

which.say: The box a process on your machine is in. A box's bar has your bar's command line, so `pgrep quickshell` can look like two desktop shells.

calibrate.say: Does this model need `--fit` to click right? A test card it reads, then the answer.

host.say: One command on your real desktop, when you asked for it: the one way past the guard, on the record.

config.say: Your settings: where windows open, confirm before closing, the bar icon, the GPU headless boxes render on.

setup.say: Links the agent skill and the bar widget, offers the guard; `--remove` undoes all of it, `--aquamarine` builds aquamarine's fix.

guard.say: Opt in, and agents' shells get a display that doesn't exist: a window they forget to box fails instead of reaching yours.

broker.say: Lets agents inside ai-jail drive boxes of their own, kept to what the jail has.

brief.say: The lines a subagent needs to drive a box, instead of the whole skill.

help.say: One command's options, its notes with `--long`, or what each exit code means.

--version.say: The version, and which aquamarine new boxes use.

look.say: Does it look right, and did it log errors? One call for an app, a shell plugin, a theme or a web page: a shot, what it shows as text and its problems, exit 1 when it found some. In the box that is up, left as it is; with none up, or `--fresh`, a throwaway box. Bare `look` reports the box now and what went wrong since the last look.

jobs.say: The box's `run -d` jobs: pid, age, processes, log and command. No `pgrep` on your host, where the same program may run on your desktop.

stop.say: Stop `run -d` jobs by the pid `jobs` lists, their windows gone, or all of them.

find.say: Where an image (a crop of an earlier shot) is on the screen or in a window, for what has no accessibility tree: a canvas, a game.

snapshot.say: Record the box HOME under a name, for `diff`: before installing, using and removing a plugin or an app.

diff.say: What was added, changed or removed in the box HOME since a snapshot, grouped by area (autostart, systemd user units, desktop entries, `~/.config`...). What a box writes on its own is left out, so an idle box diffs to nothing.

window.say: One window floated at a size, tiled, fullscreen or maximized: sets the state, never toggles it.

plugin.say: A shell plugin into a box that is already up, as `up --plugin` would, or out again.

tray.say: The box's tray items and their menus as text; open a menu, click an icon or a row over the bus, as the bar would.

dnd.say: The box's Do Not Disturb, on or off; `--clear` dismisses its toasts.

dock.say: Where Omarchy 4.5's dock takes input in the box, or turn it off so it doesn't catch clicks at the screen's edge.

polkit.say: With `up --polkit`: ask the box's polkit agent for a password, as a system service would, and say how it ended. For testing a polkit agent; it decides nothing for any service.

pid.say: The host pid of the box's Hyprland or shell, for a profiler or a debugger on your side.

doctor.say: Can this machine run boxes? Checks what a box needs and, for each thing missing, prints the line that installs it for your distribution. Changes nothing; `--smoke` also starts a box and takes a shot.
